summary: The base reproduced trailing-text stranding, multi-call stranding, and split-marker leakage. The exact candidate fixed those failures through the public FunctionCallParser stream/finalization path and restored one-shot/streaming accumulated-text equivalence in focused and independent adversarial tests.

tests.what_was_measured: Issue-specific base reproduction through FunctionCallParser: trailing text remained buffered, a second call plus surrounding text remained buffered, and a split marker leaked markup and yielded no call.

Candidate regression suite: 9 passed with 204 subtests, including public stream-end behavior, multiple calls, surrounding text, all two-chunk boundaries, split markers, and incomplete-marker EOF flushing.
Independent original-contract cases all matched one-shot results, including final call plus trailing text, two calls in one chunk with inter-call and trailing text, and a split opening marker.

1,580 deterministic chunkings comparing accumulated streaming text/calls to detect_and_parse across valid, multiple, adjacent, unknown, malformed, partial-EOF, angle-text, and newline-tail cases; all passed with empty final buffers.

gpu_execution.evidence: The issue concerns deterministic pure-Python parsing; GPU execution is not relevant to the stated contract.

remaining_limitations: No MiMo model weights or tokenizer were available or required; model semantic output and tokenizer delivery behavior were not tested.
No HTTP serving, distributed workload, or architecture-specific execution was run; verification covers the detector and public FunctionCallParser paths.
No native code changed, so no native rebuild was applicable.
